paras: The threatened lynching of Black prisoners at Shawnee, Oklahoma Territory, occurred on the evening of December 16, 1903, when citizens resolved to take "summary vengeance" on Black men arrested for a murder in the railroad yards. The sheriff and his deputies moved the prisoners to Tecumseh before dark, and no violence was reported.

On the morning of Wednesday, December 16, an unidentified white man was found dead with his throat cut in the west yards of the Choctaw railroad at Shawnee. He was tentatively identified as a drunken job-seeker who had called himself a union man. The killing came shortly after Brakeman Jas. Spence had been killed "by a negro," which the dispatch cited as a cause of local anger.

Sheriff Grace and Deputy John Hatfield arrested three Black men that morning on suspicion of connection with the murder. Car inspector Bob Dreman said he had seen four Black men with the white man at a camp fire near the stock yards about 6:30 a.m., and he identified two men arrested late Wednesday at a railroad camp west of town as part of that group. The dispatch does not say whether these two were among the first three.

That evening, according to the dispatch, "a number of citizens" aroused by the murder determined to take summary vengeance on the prisoners. Before dark the sheriff and his deputies removed the men to Tecumseh, which the paper said "frustrated the plan."
No report of charges against those who planned the attack, or of a hearing or trial of the arrested men, was found in the coverage.

The only account located is a Shawnee dispatch credited to the local News, which the Wichita Daily Eagle ran on its front page on December 19 under the headlines "Three Negroes Are Arrested" and "Men Are Removed to Thwart Possible Lynching." It treated the suspects' guilt as nearly settled, calling two of them "tough looking fellows" who were "undoubtedly at the camp fire," while reporting the planned mob action without comment and crediting the sheriff with preventing it. No Black press coverage was found.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Black prisoners at Shawnee, Oklahoma Territory
bases: A2 reports that citizens planned to 'execute summary vengeance' on Black prisoners held for a murder and that officers moved them away to 'Thwart Possible Lynching'; no violence was carried out, so this is a threatened lynching.

A2 reports a planned act of 'summary vengeance' by 'a number of citizens' in retaliation for a murder, but the sheriff removed the prisoners before dark and no one was killed, so the standard definition is not met; it was a threatened lynching.
Only one report (A2, a Wichita reprint of the Shawnee News) describes the arrests and the threat; no second white or Black press account was found.

accounts.label: Shawnee News, as reprinted by the Wichita Daily Eagle
accounts.gist: Black men were arrested on a car inspector's identification for a rail-yard murder; aroused citizens resolved on summary vengeance, but the sheriff moved the prisoners to Tecumseh before dark.

framing.detail: Reports the mob plan without comment, presents the suspects' guilt as near-certain ('undoubtedly at the camp fire', 'tough looking fellows'), and credits the sheriff with thwarting a 'Possible Lynching'.

record_check.dossier: Unnamed Black suspects: three arrested Wednesday morning plus two taken late Wednesday at the railroad camp (overlap unclear)

record_check.record: said to have been connected with the murder of an unknown man in the Choctaw yards
record_check.dossier: Suspected in the throat-cut murder of an unidentified white man in the Choctaw west yards

info: Murder discovered and first arrests made Wednesday morning, Dec. 16, 1903; the plan for vengeance formed Wednesday evening.
Shawnee, O. T.; the body was found in the west yards of the Choctaw railroad near the stock yards; prisoners removed to Tecumseh.

Unnamed Black men held on suspicion of the murder: three arrested Wednesday morning by Sheriff Grace and Deputy John Hatfield, and two arrested late Wednesday at the railroad camp west of the city; the report does not make clear whether the two were among the three or additional.
Suspected of connection with the murder of an unidentified white man found with his throat cut on the track in the Choctaw west yards.
'A number of citizens' of Shawnee, said to be aroused by the murder and by the recent killing of Brakeman Jas. Spence by a Black man.
Prisoners removed to Tecumseh and the plan 'frustrated'; no later report on the prisoners was found.
